models.scope: E. coli, polar membrane chemoreceptors/CheW/CheA, cytoplasmic CheY/CheZ, peritrichous rotary flagella. Increasing-attractant versus uniform environment.
checks: Read every zh/en stage, intro, label, control, entries metadata and all point/update formulas; no extra root contexts exist.
Stages 0/.18/.38/.56/.75/.9: correct narrative sign of attractant→lower CheA→lower CheY-P→less CW switching; adaptation is explicitly omitted, not denied.
Evaluated both control choices at every stage plus .54/.625/.8/1. Uniform branch adds tumble intervals .26–.34 and .52–.60; gradient branch preserves only .75–.83.
Inspected /tmp/atlas-refinement/chemotaxis.png at p=.55; hooks connect to modeled filaments; all motor-to-trailing-filament formulas examined.
Fixed path is labeled illustrative. Neither quantitative stochasticity nor precise motor torque is promised. Numeric tail derivative calculation gave positive handedness triple product 2295515.918.

sources.title: Darnton et al., On Torque and Tumbling in Swimming Escherichia coli
sources.supports: Opened full primary paper; Introduction and results show left-handed normal run filaments, CCW runs viewed from behind, and reversal-associated polymorphic tumble changes.

sources.title: Single-Cell E. coli Response to an Instantaneously Applied Chemotactic Signal
sources.supports: Opened primary experiment describing individual chemotactic responses; no measured trajectory is claimed by this model.

findings.evidence: All filaments use sin(t*36+p*32+f), cos(t*36+p*32+f) regardless of tumble. Tumble only widens spread and rotates the cell. For the linear trailing section, x decreases while y=sin(theta), z=cos(theta), producing right-handed geometry even in run frames; userData nevertheless says CCW-bundle or one-or-more-CW.
findings.whyWrong: The rendered reversal never occurs, and ordinary E. coli run filaments have the wrong handedness. Changing spread cannot substitute for the depicted rotary switch.
findings.fix: Build a left-handed normal run filament and give selected motor(s) continuous phase with sign reversal during tumble. Depict a selected reversed filament leaving the bundle, with an appropriate schematic polymorphic change, then returning; define the viewing convention.
findings.verification: Signed torsion must be left-handed during normal runs. Compare successive positions around each local filament axis to show at least one signed angular velocity reversal during tumble and restoration afterward; preserve root-hook continuity and absolute seeking.

limitations: The source paper notes rare reversals without chirality change; do not enforce a claim that every reversal must change chirality.
Molecular identities and pathway sign passed qualitative review; exact receptor fold, motor stoichiometry and kinetics remain schematic.

models.scope: Anaerobic E. coli NarX–NarL branch: nitrate in periplasm, inner-membrane sensor, cytoplasmic ATP/His→Asp, narGHJI transcription; active FNR assumed.
checks: Reviewed all six bilingual stages 0/.16/.34/.51/.7/.9, controls, labels, sources and shared bilayer/transcription helpers.

Both nitrate states evaluated at stage boundaries, intermediate transfer .54/.625, transcription .8 and endpoint 1. Nitrate-absent hides enhanced transfer/RNA without claiming all basal activity is absent.
Periplasm above y=.925, kinase and NarL below; two TM segments per NarX protomer and a shared nitrate pocket are consistent schematic scope.
ATP has three markers before .35 and two after; His/Asp order is correct in text, but spatial transfer and conservation fail as below.
RNA helper creates one wavy strand with its polymerase-proximal endpoint retained as length grows; DNA labels are antiparallel, but handedness is inverted.
Viewed existing p=.55 screenshot, where phosphate is visibly isolated between the proteins.

sources.title: Cheung and Hendrickson, Structural Analysis of Ligand Stimulation of NarX
sources.supports: Opened full primary structural paper: periplasmic dimer nitrate site, two TM regions, ATP-dependent His phosphorylation, NarL Asp transfer, anaerobic narGHJI control.

sources.title: Signal-Dependent Phosphorylation of Membrane-Bound NarX
sources.supports: Primary biochemical article opened successfully on first request; relevant scope is nitrate-regulated NarX phosphotransfer, not a soluble free-phosphate messenger.

sources.title: NLM MeSH: DNA, B-Form
sources.supports: Opened official definition: ordinary B-DNA is right-handed.

sources.title: NarL/DNA complex, PDB 1JE8
sources.supports: Opened primary structure record; NarL output domains contact DNA and can bend/deform its B/A geometry, not reverse the whole duplex handedness.

findings.location: update(), lines 229–251; phosphate, NarL and boundPhosphate objects
findings.evidence: During p=.46–.62, phosphate moves from (-2.12,-.4,.35) to (.4,-.6,.35), while NarL remains at (.4,-.6,.24) until p=.65. At p=.54, the marker is at (-.86,-.5,.35), far from either protein. No NarX–NarL encounter is shown. phosphate remains visible until .63 but boundPhosphate turns on at .62, producing two markers for one transferred group.
findings.whyWrong: Phosphotransfer is a direct protein encounter and group transfer. The scene instead communicates a diffusible phosphate courier and briefly duplicates the group.
findings.fix: Move NarL into contact with the NarX donor His before transfer; move the single phosphate marker only across contacting active sites; attach it to NarL after transfer and move the phosphorylated regulator toward DNA. Make visibility handoff mutually exclusive.
findings.verification: Throughout transfer, donor and acceptor sites must be within a declared contact tolerance. Account for one ATP terminal phosphate: exactly one associated transfer marker before/after handoff, including .619/.62/.625/.63.

findings.location: transcriptionDetail.point(), lines 170–177; called by twoComponentProcess.js lines 203–208
findings.evidence: At zero opening, point=(x, y+r*sin(10*(x-x0)+phase), r*cos(10*(x-x0)+phase)); x increases while transverse angle decreases around +x. The signed scalar triple product of first/second/third derivatives is negative, hence the backbone helix is left-handed. Both strands have the same chirality. This persists away from the bubble at all progress values and in the inactive control.
findings.whyWrong: The ordinary regulatory duplex is mirrored relative to B-DNA, without any Z-DNA scope.
findings.fix: Change one transverse sign (or reverse the phase progression) consistently for both backbones, phosphates and bases, preserving antiparallel endpoint labels and bubble continuity. Do not change RNA into a duplex.
findings.verification: For unopened backbone spans, a finite-difference signed-torsion test must agree with a known right-handed reference helix. Verify both strands, both conditions, and frames before/during/after activation; RNA must remain single-stranded.

limitations: NarL oligomerization, exact DNA-contact geometry, phosphatase reset and cross-regulation are not reconstructed at structural precision; this review does not approve atomistic fidelity.
Shared DNA handedness root cause is also reported for quorumSensing as bacterialSignals-04; fix the helper once.

models.scope: Aliivibrio/Vibrio fischeri LuxI–3-oxo-C6-HSL–LuxR–luxICDABEG branch, permissive other regulators/oxygen/substrates; same population under retention versus dilution.
checks: Reviewed all six bilingual stages 0/.16/.34/.51/.7/.88 and both exchange states, including every AHL path, LuxR/bound ligand state, RNA helper, extra LuxI and glow.
LuxI is cytoplasmic, LuxR is not placed in a membrane; short-chain AHL can cross the cutaway boundary. Bound markers appear only in retained activation, followed by RNA and additional LuxI.
Both branches evaluated at every stage plus .54/.625/.8/1. Dilution preserves cell count and suppresses the illustrated enhanced transcription/light.
Text explicitly qualifies oxygen, substrates and other regulatory inputs, avoiding the false claim that AHL alone guarantees light; glow is not quantified.
Viewed existing p=.55 screenshot. RNA is a single undulating chain, not a DNA-like ladder; the actual DNA ladder has the shared chirality defect.

sources.title: Urbanowski et al., Reversible AHL Binding to Purified V. fischeri LuxR
sources.supports: Opened primary abstract and figure descriptions. 3OC6-HSL-dependent LuxR binding to lux box enables transcription; dilution can reverse activation.

sources.title: Microbial Primer: LuxR-LuxI Quorum Sensing
sources.supports: Opened scholarly primer. LuxI produces signal; AHL diffusion, feedback and other permissive conditions constrain activation.

findings.evidence: At zero opening, point=(x, y+r*sin(10*(x-x0)+phase), r*cos(10*(x-x0)+phase)); x increases while transverse angle decreases around +x. The signed scalar triple product of first/second/third derivatives is negative, hence the backbone helix is left-handed. Both strands have the same chirality. This persists away from the bubble at all progress values and in the inactive control. Same helper root cause as bacterialSignals-03.
findings.whyWrong: The lux regulatory DNA is an unsupported left-handed duplex.
findings.fix: Change one transverse sign (or reverse the phase progression) consistently for both backbones, phosphates and bases, preserving antiparallel endpoint labels and bubble continuity. Do not change RNA into a duplex.
findings.verification: For unopened backbone spans, a finite-difference signed-torsion test must agree with a known right-handed reference helix. Verify both strands, both conditions, and frames before/during/after activation; RNA must remain single-stranded.

limitations: Representative AHL counts and fixed paths are not a concentration/transport simulation. Positive feedback is illustrated with added LuxI rather than explicit translation or enzyme kinetics.
Exact LuxR DNA docking, lux box sequence, heterogeneous activation times and protein atomic folds remain abstractions; no additional universal-switch claim was found.

models.scope: Nonmucoid P. aeruginosa PAO1 surface-associated aggregates, Psl/eDNA/protein matrix, optional low-level NO-associated local dispersal.
checks: Reviewed all six bilingual stages 0/.17/.34/.51/.7/.88, NO/none conditions and all cell/fiber/degradation/inset formulas.
Observed supplied p=.55 screenshot: matrix is an open fiber network, not a enclosing membrane. Species and non-universal morphology are explicit.
Evaluated both branches at all stages plus .54/.625/.8/1. Only cell indices 12/15/18/20 leave under NO; 20 of 24 representative cells remain. None branch retains cells/matrix.
Traced nearest-neighbor fiber graph: all edges incident to the four leavers are in the degradable set (12→9,15→12,18→15,20→15), so static strands do not remain falsely tethered to escaping cells.

NO arrives before local release; conceptual intracellular c-di-GMP inset shrinks. No cell killing animation occurs, consistent with the low-level cue scope; this does not prove all natural biofilm cells survive.
eDNA is distinct from polysaccharide and protein but its strand formula has reversed chirality.

sources.title: Ma et al., Assembly and development of the P. aeruginosa biofilm matrix
sources.supports: Opened primary abstract/figures: Psl scaffolding and spatially heterogeneous matrix, eDNA and mobile versus retained populations.

sources.title: Barraud et al., NO signaling, phosphodiesterase activity and dispersal
sources.supports: Opened primary abstract/figures: low non-toxic NO promotes PDE activity, lower c-di-GMP and dispersal.

findings.evidence: For each eDNA fiber, x increases with j, while y=y0+.045*sin(.7*j+phase) and z=.68+.045*cos(.7*j+phase). This produces left-handed double helices in all six eDNA objects whenever visible, in both conditions.
findings.whyWrong: Ordinary chromosomal eDNA is depicted with the opposite handedness without a special DNA-form scope.
findings.fix: Reverse one transverse sign or angular progression for both eDNA strands, preserving base-pair links and the external matrix compartment.
findings.verification: Evaluate signed torsion of every visible eDNA backbone against a right-handed reference at mature and dispersal frames in both conditions; strand links must remain paired and extracellular.

limitations: Metabolic/oxygen gradients, dormancy, cell lysis and eDNA production are omitted. The explicit representative-cell and selected-route language avoids claiming uniform biology.
Matrix molecular repeats are schematic motifs, not exact Psl chemistry. Low-level NO response is a selected case, not a guarantee for every biofilm.
